# Sampling - Practice Test - Year 8

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

State whether each set of data is primary data or secondary data.

(a) You measure the heights of the students in your class.

(b) You download rainfall figures from the Bureau of Meteorology website.

(c) You hand out a survey you wrote and collect the answers.

(d) You use population figures printed in a newspaper article.

**Question 2**

State whether each sampling method is random or non-random.

(a) Drawing $20$ names out of a hat that holds the names of every student in the school.

(b) Asking the first $20$ people who walk into a shopping centre.

(c) Choosing every $10$th name on the school roll, starting from a name picked at random among the first $10$.

(d) An online poll that anyone can choose to answer.

**Question 3**

Ten students were chosen at random and asked how many pets they have. Their answers were:

$$0, \ 2, \ 1, \ 3, \ 1, \ 0, \ 1, \ 4, \ 2, \ 1$$

Find the mean, median, mode and range.

**Question 4**

A club has a numbered list of $500$ members. The secretary wants a systematic sample of $25$ members.

(a) How many members apart should the chosen members be on the list?

(b) If the first member chosen is number $7$, write the numbers of the first four members chosen.

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

Name the sampling method used in each case. Choose from: simple random, systematic, stratified, convenience, voluntary response.

(a) The names of all $800$ students are entered into a computer, which randomly picks $40$ of them.

(b) A school randomly chooses $10$ students from each year level.

(c) A reporter interviews people waiting at the bus stop outside her office.

(d) A radio station asks listeners to text in their opinion.

**Question 6**

A school has $300$ Year 7, $280$ Year 8, $260$ Year 9 and $160$ Year 10 students. The principal wants a stratified sample of $50$ students, with each year level represented in the same proportion as in the school.

How many students should be chosen from each year level?

**Question 7**

A radio station asks listeners to phone in and say whether a new freeway should be built through their city. Of the people who called, $85\%$ said "no".

Explain why this result may not represent the views of the people in the city.

**Question 8**

The students in a class are numbered $01$ to $40$. A teacher uses this row of random digits to choose a sample of five students:

$$27 \ 81 \ 05 \ 27 \ 39 \ 64 \ 12 \ 33 \ 18$$

She reads the digits two at a time, ignores any number greater than $40$ and ignores any number that repeats. Which five students are chosen?

**Question 9**

A random sample of $15$ Year 8 students sat a test marked out of $80$. Their marks were:

$$56, \ 41, \ 63, \ 52, \ 70, \ 48, \ 56, \ 61, \ 45, \ 76, \ 53, \ 58, \ 64, \ 55, \ 67$$

(a) Draw a stem-and-leaf plot of the marks, with the leaves in order.

(b) Find the median, mode and range.

**Question 10**

A student finds this table of a town's average monthly rainfall, in millimetres, on a weather website.

| Month | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun | Jul | Aug | Sep | Oct | Nov | Dec |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rainfall (mm) | 40 | 35 | 50 | 55 | 70 | 80 | 85 | 80 | 65 | 60 | 55 | 45 |

(a) Is this primary or secondary data?

(b) Find the range.

(c) Find the median monthly rainfall.

(d) Find the mean monthly rainfall.

**Question 11**

A random sample of $20$ games was chosen from a soccer league's season. The number of goals scored in each game is shown in the table.

| Goals in the game | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of games | 3 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 2 |

Find:

(a) the mode

(b) the median

(c) the mean

**Question 12**

A random sample of $9$ students recorded how much they earned from part-time work last week:

\$60, \$75, \$80, \$80, \$90, \$95, \$100, \$110, \$480

(a) Find the mean and the median.

(b) Which measure, the mean or the median, better describes a typical amount in this sample? Explain.

**Question 13**

A factory makes $6000$ cans of soup in a shift. To check quality, it picks one of the first $50$ cans at random, then checks every $50$th can after that.

(a) How many cans are checked in a shift?

(b) Name this type of sampling.

(c) Give one possible problem with this method.

**Question 14**

A random sample of $40$ students from a school of $900$ were asked how many hours of screen time they had yesterday. The results are shown in the table.

| Hours of screen time | 0 to less than 2 | 2 to less than 4 | 4 to less than 6 | 6 to less than 8 | 8 to less than 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students | 6 | 15 | 11 | 6 | 2 |

(a) Which class is the modal class?

(b) What percentage of the sample had $6$ or more hours of screen time?

(c) Which class contains the median?

(d) Estimate the number of students in the school who had less than $2$ hours of screen time.

**Question 15**

A school wants to survey $30$ students about the canteen menu. Four methods are suggested.

Method A: Ask the first $30$ students in the canteen queue.

Method B: Draw $30$ names at random from a list of every student in the school.

Method C: Put up a notice asking for $30$ volunteers.

Method D: Ask the $30$ students in the principal's maths class.

(a) Which method is best? Explain.

(b) Give a reason why Method A could give a biased result.

**Question 16**

A health website states that the mean height of $13$-year-olds is about $158 \text{ cm}$. Jess measures the heights of a random sample of $8$ students in her year level:

$$150, \ 162, \ 155, \ 160, \ 158, \ 149, \ 165, \ 157$$

(a) Is the website's figure primary or secondary data? Is Jess's data primary or secondary?

(b) Find the mean height of Jess's sample.

(c) Find the range of Jess's sample.

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

A gym has $1200$ members: $480$ are under $30$, $540$ are aged $30$ to $50$, and $180$ are over $50$. The manager takes a stratified sample of $80$ members, with each age group represented in the same proportion as in the gym.

(a) How many members from each age group should be in the sample?

(b) The sample results for "Do you want longer opening hours?" were:

| Age group | Under 30 | 30 to 50 | Over 50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Number who said yes | 24 | 18 | 3 |

For each age group, use the sample to estimate how many of the gym's members in that group want longer opening hours.

(c) Estimate the total number of members who want longer opening hours.

**Question 18**

A council wants to know how many of the $16\,000$ adults in its town use the local library at least once a month. Two samples of $100$ adults were taken.

Method 1: $100$ people inside the library were surveyed. $92$ said they use the library at least once a month.

Method 2: $100$ adults were chosen at random from a list of all adults in the town. $23$ said they use the library at least once a month.

(a) Which method is biased? Explain why.

(b) Use the better sample to estimate the number of adults in the town who use the library at least once a month.

(c) How much bigger is the estimate from Method 1 than the estimate in part (b)?

**Question 19**

A random sample of $25$ families in a suburb were asked how many cars they own.

| Number of cars | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of families | 2 | 8 | 10 | 4 | 1 |

(a) Find the mean number of cars per family.

(b) Find the median number of cars per family.

(c) The suburb has $3000$ families. Estimate the total number of cars owned by families in the suburb.

(d) Estimate the number of families in the suburb with no car.

**Question 20**

Zara wants to estimate the mean number of hours of homework the $450$ Year 8 students at her school do each week. She asks her $6$ closest friends, who answer:

$$8, \ 10, \ 9, \ 12, \ 11, \ 10$$

(a) Find the mean of Zara's sample.

(b) Name the type of sampling Zara used.

(c) Give two reasons why her estimate may not be reliable.

(d) Describe a better way for Zara to choose her sample.

# Sampling - Answer Key

**Question 1**

Answer: (a) Primary (b) Secondary (c) Primary (d) Secondary

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) Random (b) Non-random (c) Random (d) Non-random

**Question 3**

Answer: Mean $1.5$ ($15 \div 10$), median $1$, mode $1$, range $4$

**Question 4**

Answer: (a) Every $20$th member ($500 \div 25$) (b) $7, 27, 47, 67$

**Question 5**

Answer: (a) Simple random (b) Stratified (c) Convenience (d) Voluntary response

**Question 6**

Answer: Year 7: $15$, Year 8: $14$, Year 9: $13$, Year 10: $8$ (each year level's number $\times \frac{50}{1000}$)

**Question 7**

Answer: It is a voluntary response sample: only people who listen to that station, and who feel strongly enough to call (often people who are against the idea), are included, so the sample is biased.

**Question 8**

Answer: Students $27, 05, 39, 12, 33$ ($81$ and $64$ are too big, the second $27$ is a repeat)

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) Stem 4: leaves 1 5 8; stem 5: leaves 2 3 5 6 6 8; stem 6: leaves 1 3 4 7; stem 7: leaves 0 6 (key: $4 | 1$ means $41$) (b) Median $56$, mode $56$, range $35$

**Question 10**

Answer: (a) Secondary (b) $50 \text{ mm}$ ($85 - 35$) (c) $57.5 \text{ mm}$ ($\frac{55 + 60}{2}$) (d) $60 \text{ mm}$ ($720 \div 12$)

**Question 11**

Answer: (a) $1$ goal (b) $2$ goals (10th and 11th values are both $2$) (c) $1.8$ goals ($36 \div 20$)

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) Mean \$130 ($1170 \div 9$), median \$90 (b) The median, because the outlier of \$480 pulls the mean up so that it is higher than $8$ of the $9$ amounts.

**Question 13**

Answer: (a) $120$ cans ($6000 \div 50$) (b) Systematic sampling (c) For example: if a fault happens in a regular pattern (such as every $50$th can, or every $25$th can), the checks could miss it or always land on it.

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) 2 to less than 4 hours (b) $20\%$ ($\frac{8}{40}$) (c) 2 to less than 4 hours (the 20th and 21st values are both in this class) (d) $135$ students ($\frac{6}{40} \times 900$)

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) Method B, because it is a random sample where every student has the same chance of being chosen, so it is most likely to represent the school. (b) Students in the canteen queue already buy from the canteen, so they may like the menu more than students who never use it.

**Question 16**

Answer: (a) The website's figure is secondary data; Jess's data is primary data. (b) $157 \text{ cm}$ ($1256 \div 8$) (c) $16 \text{ cm}$ ($165 - 149$)

**Question 17**

Answer: (a) Under 30: $32$, 30 to 50: $36$, over 50: $12$ (b) Under 30: $360$ ($\frac{24}{32} \times 480$), 30 to 50: $270$ ($\frac{18}{36} \times 540$), over 50: $45$ ($\frac{3}{12} \times 180$) (c) $675$ members

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) Method 1, because everyone surveyed was already at the library, so library users are over-represented. (b) $3680$ adults ($\frac{23}{100} \times 16\,000$) (c) $11\,040$ more (Method 1 gives $\frac{92}{100} \times 16\,000 = 14\,720$)

**Question 19**

Answer: (a) $1.76$ ($44 \div 25$) (b) $2$ (the 13th value) (c) $5280$ cars ($1.76 \times 3000$) (d) $240$ families ($\frac{2}{25} \times 3000$)

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) $10$ hours ($60 \div 6$) (b) Convenience sampling (non-random) (c) Any two of: the sample is very small; it is not random; her friends are likely to be similar to each other (for example in the same classes) and may not represent all Year 8 students. (d) Choose a larger random sample, for example $40$ names drawn at random from a list of all $450$ Year 8 students.
